title: Spread out finite-type nearby-cycle input to an arithmetic base
statement: Let $S$ be integral affine Noetherian, $f:X\to S$ of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\Lambda$ finite with $m\Lambda=0$ and $m$ invertible on $S$, and $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ have constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. There exist an integral affine scheme $S_0$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z[1/m]$, a dominant map $a:S\to S_0$, a finite-type morphism $f_0:X_0\to S_0$, and $K_0\in D^b_c(X_{0,\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$, with $X\simeq X_0\times_{S_0}S$ and $K\simeq a_X^*K_0$. The scheme $S_0$ is excellent Noetherian and finite-dimensional. If $q_0:S'_0\to S_0$ is a modification, the reduced closure $S'$ of its isomorphism open after base change to $S$ is a modification $q:S'\to S$ and maps to $S'_0$. For every integer $r$, $P_r((f_0)_{S'_0},(K_0)_{S'_0})$ implies $P_r(f_{S'},K_{S'})$, with $P_r$ and modification as in [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data].

source.place: §2.1, p. 3 (finite-presentation and constructible-complex descent, dominant arithmetic model, strict transform); Lu--Zheng proof of Theorem 4.27 for general coefficients. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Write S=Spec(A). Since m is a unit in A, regard A as a filtered colimit of finitely generated integral Z[1/m]-subalgebras. The affine inverse-system presentation of S by finite-type integer stages and the finite-type ring factorization lemma let us choose an integral affine S_0=Spec(A_0), finite type over Z[1/m], and a dominant map a:S→S_0. The inclusion A_0→A is injective because A is a domain, hence a is dominant.

source.place: §2.1, p. 3: dominant arithmetic model and finite-presentation descent.

proof.text: Because S is Noetherian and f is finite type, X is Noetherian. Hence X is quasi-separated. Since S is affine, this makes f quasi-separated: intersections of affine opens in X are quasi-compact. The finite-type hypothesis already gives quasi-compactness of f. Over locally Noetherian S, the locally finite-type f is locally finitely presented. Thus f is of finite presentation, using the locally-finitely-presented, quasi-compact and quasi-separated criterion. Each arithmetic S_j is finite type over Z, hence Noetherian and qcqs by the same Noetherianity and quasi-separatedness lemmas. Apply clause (1) of thm-pd-spreading-out to the arithmetic inverse system of step 1. It gives a stage i and a finitely presented f_i:X_i→S_i with X≅X_i×_{S_i}S. In particular f_i is finite type. This uses a general existence theorem, with no unprovided Nagata gluing data.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (1); Properties 01OY and Morphisms 01TP for finite presentation over the Noetherian base.

proof.text: For j≥i put X_j=X_i×_{S_i}S_j. Affine charts base change by tensor product, preserving the finite generators; so X_j is finite type over S_j and Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma (each S_j is finite type over Z). Each X_j is qcqs, by Noetherianity and the quasi-separatedness lemma. The transition maps are affine, because on an affine chart they are base changes of maps between affine S_j. The universal property of fibre products identifies X with lim X_j. Choose a≤b with H^q(K)=0 outside [a,b]. Descend the finitely many constructible sheaves H^q(K) using constructible-module-limit-descent and pass to a common stage, writing their models as M_q. Pullback along a transition g:X_{j'}→X_j preserves their constructibility as Λ-modules: take a stratification (ι_k:Z_k→X_j) witnessing constructibility of M_q, with Λ-linear trivializations ι_k^{-1}M_q|_{U}≅\underline{M} on an etale cover; the strata g^{-1}(T_k) are locally closed, and constructible since X_{j'} is Noetherian (a locally closed subset of a Noetherian space is constructible; constructible-etale-set-pullback gives the same for the underlying finite abelian sheaves in general); the restriction of g^{-1}M_q to Z_k×_{X_j}X_{j'} is the inverse image of ι_k^{-1}M_q, and the inverse image of the constant Λ-module sheaf \underline{M} on U is the constant Λ-module sheaf \underline{M} on U×_{X_j}X_{j'}, so the pulled-back trivializations are Λ-linear on the pulled-back etale cover. Thus all the hypotheses for the bounded derived-Hom continuity node apply to this system.

source.place: Tag 09YU (3), lemma-category-is-colimit: essential surjectivity for constructible module sheaves; finite common-stage selection.

proof.text: Use exactness of site inverse image: the same holds on constant-Λ modules, since kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels with induced Λ-actions. Therefore inverse image acts termwise on the derived category, is triangulated by the exact-functor lemma, and commutes with H^q and smart truncations (kernels and images commute with this exact functor). Write T_q=τ_{≤q}K; the successive truncation-triangle lemma gives exactly T_{q-1}→T_q→H^q(K)[-q]→T_{q-1}[1]. Start with L_{a-1}=0 modeling T_{a-1}=0. For q=a,...,b suppose a bounded constructible L_{q-1} and an inverse-image isomorphism L_{q-1}|_X≅T_{q-1} have been constructed. Under this isomorphism and M_q|_X≅H^q(K), the connecting arrow is a morphism δ_q:M_q|_X[-q]→L_{q-1}|_X[1]. Apply bounded derived-Hom continuity with P=M_q[-q], Q=L_{q-1}, n=1. Its colimit surjectivity represents δ_q by δ_{q,j}:M_{q,j}[-q]→L_{q-1,j}[1] at a later stage j.

source.place: Tags 015F and 08J5; agent finite Postnikov induction for the complex-descent assertion of Orgogozo §2.1.

proof.text: Take a cone of δ_{q,j} and rotate/shift its distinguished triangle to obtain L_{q-1,j}→L_{q,j}→M_{q,j}[-q]→L_{q-1,j}[1], with L_{q,j}=Cone(δ_{q,j})[-1] and the appropriate rotation signs. The cohomology long exact sequence gives H^q(L_{q,j})≅M_{q,j}, H^t(L_{q,j})≅H^t(L_{q-1,j}) for t<q, and zero outside [a,q]; hence L_{q,j} is bounded constructible. On X the transported connecting arrow equals the one for T_q, by choice of δ_{q,j}. TR3 applied after rotation gives a morphism from the pulled-back triangle to the truncation triangle, with the prescribed isomorphisms on T_{q-1} and H^q(K)[-q]. The two-isomorphisms lemma makes its middle component an isomorphism L_{q,j}|_X≅T_q. This closes the induction. After its finitely many stage enlargements take K_0=L_b and S_0,X_0 at the final stage. Since T_b≅K, K_0|_X≅K. This constructs cones of derived morphisms, without assuming constructible terms or a bounded projective representative of K.

source.place: TR1–TR3 in Tag 0145; cohomology exactness in Tag 05RS and the homological-functor definition 0147; Tag 014A for two isomorphisms. Agent finite Postnikov construction.

proof.text: The final A_0=Γ(S_0,O) is finite type over Z: adjoin 1/m and the finitely many Z[1/m]-algebra generators. The integer ring is excellent by lem-trf-integers-excellent, and its finite-type algebra A_0 is excellent by lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent with multiplicative subset {1}. Excellence includes Noetherianity by def-exc-excellent-ring. Every principal affine open Spec(A_0[1/t]) also has excellent coordinate ring by the same localization lemma; these opens form an affine basis, so S_0 is excellent. Noetherianity of S_0 also follows directly from the finite-type-over-Z scheme lemma.

source.place: Tags 07QW (3) and 07QU; excellence and its finite-type/localization stability.

proof.text: For dimension, every ideal J of Z is principal: J=0 or choose its least positive element d; Euclidean division by d leaves a remainder in J smaller than d, hence remainder zero. The principal-ideal-ring dimension bound gives dim Z≤1. Excellence already gives Noetherianity of Z. Choose a surjection Z[t_1,...,t_N]→A_0 from its finite set of ring generators. By the Noetherian polynomial-dimension theorem the source has dimension dim Z+N≤N+1. The inverse images of a strict prime chain in A_0 form a strict prime chain in the polynomial ring: inverse images are prime, and surjectivity reflects equality of inverse-image ideals. Thus dim A_0≤N+1, and the ring dimension definition identifies this with dim S_0. This bound does not require Z→A_0 to be injective and applies unchanged to positive characteristic.

source.place: MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_of_isNoetherianRing:120–121; PID.lean:20–21 for the base bound, and elementary prime-chain pullback under the polynomial presentation.

proof.text: Let q_0:S'_{0}→S_0 be a modification in the current definition of def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data, with dense isomorphism open U_0⊂S_0. Put U=a^{-1}(U_0) and Y=S×_{S_0}S'_{0}. The generic point of integral S maps to the generic point of integral S_0 by dominance, and the latter lies in U_0. Thus U contains the generic point of S and is dense in S. Over U the proper base change Y→S is an isomorphism. Let S' be the reduced closure of this open copy of U in Y. It is closed in Y and hence proper over S by the two properness lemmas. Restriction of the reduced closure to U is U itself, since U is reduced as an open of integral S. Therefore q:S'→S is an isomorphism over the dense open U of its target. Its inverse image of U is dense in S' by the closure construction. The resulting q is finite type, since it is proper; its source S' is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma. These are both density requirements in the current modification definition, so q is a modification. The second projection restricted to S' gives S'→S'_0.

source.place: §2.1, p. 3: strict transform/reduced closure of the dense isomorphism open.

proof.text: Fix r and assume P_r((f_0)_{S'_0},(K_0)_{S'_0}). For any T→S' and T'→T, use the composite T→S'→S'_0 as the preliminary base change in this P_r hypothesis, and use the same T'→T as its further base change. The fibre-product universal property identifies X_{S'}×_{S'}T with X_0×_{S_0}T and similarly over T'; the coefficients identify by the already constructed inverse-image isomorphism for K. Thus the ordinary comparison for (f_{S'},K_{S'}) over T'→T is exactly the comparison covered by this instance of the hypothesis. Its cone has H^i=0 for i≤r. Since T and T' were arbitrary, this is P_r(f_{S'},K_{S'}). No identification of nearby cycles with an arbitrary pullback from S'_0 is used: both comparisons are for the same T-family and T'→T.
